newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks fall in quiet local trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks fall in quiet local trade.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell 0.11 percent in quiet trade with little foreign buying, brokers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.18 points to 161.11 points in trade worth just 874,000 dinars ($1.23 million), the lowest turnover in nearly three weeks.
Blue-chip stocks which have underpinned the market in recent weeks were little traded.
Jordan Cement Factories, targeted by foreign investors on Saturday and Sunday, fell 0.01 dinars to 4.08 dinars after shares worth 90,000 dinars traded.

Arab Bank and Jordan Islamic Bank closed unchanged at 263 dinars and 3.76 dinars on Monday. Both banks had risen in busy trade last week on expectation of a surge in demand if the cabinet approves plans to lift a 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling on stocks.
"If the approval goes ahead those shares will rise again," said broker Ibrahim Odeh.
Falling shares outnumbered gainers on Monday by 14 to four, with another 22 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.32 percent to 80.70 points, 3.22 percent down from the start of the year.
